title: Cleanup concordance runbook (draft)
body: Purpose: This is a personal runbook for labeling / cleanup heuristics I keep returning to when triaging long-tail concordance issues. Mostly a scratchpad for quick decisions in the adjudication UI and for writing batch cleanup scripts (python + jq). Scope: - Small-medium corpora (10k-2M rows) for ingestion into embeddings/semantic search or downstream model evals. - Tasks: entity tagging, canonicalization, dedupe, token-boundary fixes, punctuation noise. - Not a full production spec — intended to capture recurring edgecases and a default escalation path. Quick rules (TL;DR): 1) Prefer conservative splits: if unsure between two adjacent spans, choose the smaller span as the labeled entity, mark the other as CONTEXT. 2) Abbreviations with trailing dot (e.g., "U.S.") -> canonical form: "US" unless doc-level evidence preserves punctuation. 3) Email-like tokens inside free text: do not tag as ORG unless company name clearly present (use CONTACT or leave untagged). 4) Numeric ranges: tag each numeric token separately; range connectors ("-", "to") are NOT part of the numeric span unless explicitly required. Representative edgecases and adjudication notes: - Case: "Acme Labs, Inc./Acme Labs Inc" Decision: canonical -> "Acme Labs"; both variants map to same ID. Keep original punctuation in provenance metadata. - Case: HTML fragments inside descriptions: "urgent Acme" Heuristic: strip safe tags prior to tokenization for labeling; annotate recovered HTML in metadata so we can restore if needed. - Case: concatenated identifiers: "ORDER#123ABC" Tagging: split into LABEL: ORDER_ID = "123ABC" and keep prefix as type token. If downstream embedding should hide boilerplate, add flag "mask_for_embeddings". - Case: emoji-heavy utterances: "Thanks! 🙏" Rule: emojis are metadata. Only tag as non-linguistic signals (REACTION) when they carry intent (e.g., thumbs-up following a question = affirmation). Tokenization pitfalls we've hit: - Byte-level vs. whitespace tokenizers lead to different boundaries on hyphenated product names. Always use the canonical tokenizer defined in the ingestion pipeline (see linked GH PR). - Multi-byte punctuation (em-dash) shows up as separate token in some tokenizers; run quick normalizer: em-dash -> " - ". Dedup / concordance heuristics: - Step 1: exact normalized string dedupe (lowercase, collapse whitespace, strip diacritics). Keep earliest created_at row unless provenance indicates higher confidence. - Step 2: soft-dedupe via fuzzy ratio (token_set_ratio > 92) but only within same source. For cross-source fuzzy matches, escalate to manual review queue. - Step 3: if embeddings distance < 0.12 (cosine) AND fuzzy ratio > 85, flag as probable duplicate; auto-merge only if both rows have identical label sets. Adjudication checklist (what to mark during pair review): - [ ] Is the canonical form unambiguous? - [ ] Are there URL fragments that got tokenized into entity spans? Remove if yes. - [ ] Is this a brand variant (subsidiary vs parent)? If yes, create mapping table and add to canonical_aliases.csv. Examples for quick copy-paste into adjudication comments: - "Canonical -> 'Acme Labs' (remove legal suffix), provenance: original 'Acme Labs, Inc.' source: dataset-x line 1243." - "Merged with 'Acme Labs Ltd' after manual review; kept earliest created_at; reason: identical org web domain present." Data-cleanup snippets I run often (pseudo): - Normalize whitespace: sed -E 's/\u00A0/ /g' | python -c "import sys,unicodedata; print(unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', sys.stdin.read()))" - Abbrev expansion: small lookup map (e.g., "co." -> "company") applied only when token frequency indicates likely company context. Open questions / TODOs: - Should we keep punctuation in canonical forms for legal records? (ex: "Smith & Co., LLP") - Proposal: preserve punctuation only if it changes search/parse results (run A/B on recall for queries containing punctuation). - How to best capture multi-lingual diacritics policy? For now: canonicalize to NFKC but store original_raw for provenance. - Build small UI widget to mark "mask_for_embeddings" during adjudication. Worth a quick prototype? Notes to self (shortcuts): - linear INF-4123 = sample curation for concordance run. - GH PR updates tokenization tests for em-dash + url-split. Run unit tests locally before big merges. - If fuzzy merges >500 rows, switch to batched manual sampling; set sample size = min(500, sqrt(n)). References and patterns I've found useful: - "Prefer fewer false merges": conservative merge policy reduces downstream data-ops surprises. - Keep canonical_aliases.csv in repo and auto-generate a 'confidence' column after each batch run. If you find contradictions in the adjudication UI, add a line comment and ping @Jonah (he's maintaining the adjudicator heuristics). -- end of runbook scratchpad -- Revision log: 2025-02-10 initial notes; 2025-02-24 fleshed dedupe heuristics; 2025-03-01 added embedding-distance rule and open questions.
